display.purpose: The home masthead and nothing else. Fraunces 720, oldstyle numerals (text-display).

card-title.purpose: A post's title on a draft sheet or row, a dialog title (text-card-title). A subsection step exists at 1.075rem / 560 (text-subsection).

body.purpose: Reading text. Lead paragraphs use 1.125rem with text-pretty; descriptions 0.875-1rem in Ink Muted.

label.purpose: The wall label (label-mono): kickers, dates, word counts, the catalogue line under a draft sheet, footer column heads, pricing figures. Uppercase, tracked, tabular numerals, Ink Muted.

shadows.name: header-sheet
shadows.purpose: The sticky header only, so it reads as a separate sheet when content scrolls under it. One of the two sanctioned shadows.

shadows.name: cta-ledge
shadows.purpose: The primary button (cta-primary) only: a 1px ledge beneath its border so the one filled button feels pressed onto the page. Removed when disabled. No other content surface carries a shadow at rest or on hover.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Button, field and link colour/border transitions (--duration-fast).

motion.name: duration-default
motion.purpose: Tailwind default transition duration; plate border warming (--duration-default).

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Every hover and focus transition on the notebook utilities.

motion.name: cta-press
motion.purpose: Primary and secondary buttons press one pixel down.

motion.name: ink-underline
motion.value: transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) from the left
motion.purpose: A link's underline scored in under the cursor or focus ring. The site's only authored motion; none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation-duration and transition-duration 0.01ms; loaders (animate-pulse, animate-spin) slow to 3s instead of stopping
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion policy. 0.01ms rather than 0s so transitionend still fires.

motion.name: dialog-toast
motion.value: 200-300ms opacity (and 95%->100% scale) via Headless UI Transition / framer-motion
motion.purpose: A dialog or a toast arriving. The interface, not content.

narrative.overview:
Blog AI is a manuscript in progress. Every post, book and template is a sheet of paper pasted into a working notebook: a square draft sheet, a title in serif, a catalogue line in mono underneath (words · tone · date). Every generated draft is the next page, and the only saturated thing on any page is the ink the editor marks it with.

The notebook is the same stationery as lscaturchio.xyz and InfiniStar, by design: warm off-white paper with a near-invisible grain, structure drawn with hairlines and space rather than boxes, a serif with personality for what the site says, a plain sans for what the reader reads, and a monospace label beside every piece of metadata. What tells the three notebooks apart is the pen. The personal site writes in forest green, InfiniStar in mulberry; Blog AI writes in Iron Gall, the blue-black ink that manuscripts were actually written in — the editor's pen on the draft.

What Blog AI keeps that the sibling sites do not have: the draft sheet as the recurring unit of the work, hairline-divided rows for history, templates and tools, and a working surface of forms, generators and settings that the notebook language extends to.

The system deliberately is not three things. It is not the amber-on-cream SaaS it replaced: no body gradient, no radial orbs behind the hero, no glass cards, no glow or lift shadows, no sparkle pill, no sections that fade in as you scroll. It is not landing-page chrome: no three-column feature tiles, no badge pills as decoration. And it is not a palette: every Tailwind hue that used to be reached for directly is being driven to zero by a ratchet, and colour arrives through the tokens.
keyCharacteristics: One paper ground, warm off-white with a fixed 3.5% noise grain; dark mode is a night variant of the same page.
One ink, Iron Gall, spent sparingly: links, hover, selection, the focus ring, the single primary button per view.
Hairline rules and tint shifts structure the page; there are no floating cards and no decorative shadows.
Three type voices with fixed jobs: Fraunces speaks, Instrument Sans reads, IBM Plex Mono catalogues.
Squareness marks the work (draft sheets); roundness marks the interface (controls, chips).
Motion is the interface responding to the reader, never the page introducing itself.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Iron Gall is the only chromatic accent on any surface, and it marks action or emphasis, never area. If a screen has the ink in more than a few places, it has too many. No gradient anywhere, on anything.

rules.name: The Sand Hairline Rule
rules.body: Dividers are 1px of Hairline, sand-toned, never neutral grey and never thicker. Depth of structure is expressed by more rules and more space, not by darker lines.

rules.name: The Tinted Paper Rule
rules.body: A "contained" surface is the same paper at a different tint (Paper Card lighter, Paper Tinted darker), bordered by a hairline. It is never a white box on a grey page.

rules.name: The Wall Label Rule
rules.body: Every piece of metadata (a date, a count, a tone, a category) is set as a Label: mono, small, uppercase, tracked, muted. Metadata never borrows the body or heading voice. Every section, row and figure introduces itself with one before its title; the kicker is the house device.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Rule
rules.body: Fraunces appears only where the site is speaking: h1-h6, the type-scale utilities, the wordmark, titles on draft sheets, stat numerals. Never in body copy, UI controls, generated drafts or labels. font-display on a non-heading fails the build unless the element carries data-voice="display".

rules.name: The Fluid Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings scale with clamp(), not breakpoints; weights step down the hierarchy (720 → 700 → 650 → 620 → 560) and tracking loosens as size falls. A leading-* class is honoured over a responsive text-* size, so write the line-height you mean.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No shadow on any content surface, at rest or on hover. A hovered surface changes tint and border colour; it does not rise.

rules.name: The Two Sheets Rule
rules.body: The only elevated objects are the sticky header and the primary button 1px ledge. Nothing else may add a shadow without changing this file first.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: A modal separates with a scrim, not a shadow. overlay-scrim (hsl(var(--scrim) / var(--scrim-alpha)), ink in both themes, 25% on paper and 55% at night) is the third sanctioned separation mechanism, and the only one available to an overlay.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Running text, including generated drafts, caps at 65-75 characters per line, measured in the DOM, not assumed from the unit.

dos: Do introduce every section, row and figure with a wall label before its title.
Do divide with 1px sand hairlines and 64-96px of vertical space; let whitespace and rules do the structuring.
Do spend Iron Gall on action and emphasis only: links, hover, selection, one primary button per view.
Do build text-led lists as stacked hairline-divided rows and keep previews as square draft sheets in a gallery grid.
Do route every colour through the tokens; status is text-success, text-warning, text-info, text-destructive and their -muted washes.
Do keep numerals tabular in labels and oldstyle in display, and set every date and count in mono.
Do design dark mode as the same notebook at night: cool hue-220 page, the ink lifted to 224 55% 76%, hairlines at 18% lightness.
Do give an empty section an honest empty state in the same voice: a wall label, one serif line, one primary action.
Do set generated drafts in the body sans at the reading measure; the serif is for what the site says, not what the model wrote.
donts: Don't add shadows to content surfaces at rest or on hover; the header sheet and the CTA ledge are the only elevated objects.
Don't reintroduce gradients, glow, blurred blooms, orbs or glass cards; the amber era is gone.
Don't build SaaS furniture: three-column feature tiles, pill badges as decoration, sparkle icons.
Don't use monospace as a voice. It is the label beside the work, never headings or body copy; the site is not a terminal.
Don't set Fraunces in body text, controls, drafts or labels, and don't set body copy in anything but Instrument Sans.
Don't use neutral grey for rules or muted surfaces; every neutral is warm paper (hue 30-38) in light mode and cool night (hue 220) in dark.
Don't introduce a second accent colour; Iron Gall Soft exists for secondary fills and the four signal colours are for status only.
Don't round a draft sheet or scale it on hover; squareness marks the work.
Don't define --spacing-xs..4xl tokens in @theme; in Tailwind v4 they shadow the max-w-* container scale and collapse layouts.
Don't animate content in, and don't ship a skeleton that a reader without JavaScript would keep.
